name: Phase-Lagged Relational Closure

replaces_or_refines.note: Does not assert triads are required; treats triadic/odd structure as one possible projection of non-canceling phase residue.

core_dependency.reading: Nonzero distinction persists only through residue-conditioned admissible continuation.

candidate_statement.plain: Stable closure requires recurring relational distinction with non-canceling phase residue. A third node is not required; the effective third term may be phase lag generated by finite propagation between relational poles.
candidate_statement.condition: Δφ_R ≠ 0 and Δφ_R does not collapse into perfect cancellation.

key_shift.from: Closure requires at least three nodes or triadic topology.
key_shift.to: Closure requires non-canceling phase-lagged recurrence in a relation.

terms.D(A|B)_φ: Directed distinction relation with phase signature φ.
terms.Δφ_R: Residue-bearing phase lag produced by finite propagation / non-instantaneous reciprocal influence.
terms.closure: Persistence of nonzero relational distinction through recurrence.

non_claims: Does not claim triads are false.
Does not claim dyads are always stable.
Does not claim phase lag is a physical signal delay.
Does not promote K as universal.
allowed_interpretation: Triads may appear as a projected or discrete realization of phase-lagged closure.
Odd parity may be a projection of non-canceling phase residue.
Dyadic systems may close when reciprocal influence contains admissible phase lag.

failure_modes.description: Δφ_R collapses to zero; recurrence becomes instantaneous symmetry and loses closure distinction.
Phase relation produces perfect cancellation rather than persistent nonzero distinction.
Phase lag does not condition future recurrence; closure is memoryless and not ra-valid.
The relation fails to recur through an admissible path.

testable_predictions.statement: Closure stability should correlate more strongly with non-canceling phase-lag residue than with node count.
Dyadic systems with controlled non-canceling phase lag should sustain closure where zero-lag dyads fail.
Triadic closure should lose special status when phase-lag conditions are matched.
Removing residue from phase lag should reduce identity-like recurrence even if topology is preserved.

recommended_attack.attack_goal: Determine whether phase-lagged recurrence is load-bearing or merely another description of generic attractor dynamics.

promotion_blockers: formal definition of phase signature φ
metric distinguishing phase-lag closure from generic attractor stability
